title: Build with Max AI

text: Build with Max AI # Compose the capabilities your application needs from explicit, replaceable components. Connect tools Give an agent typed Python functions or native tools to use. Remember users Store user and session context with local, SQLite, or MongoDB memory. Search knowledge Retrieve relevant reference material only when the agent needs it. title: Agent
summary: Agent is the coordinator for one configured assistant. It combines identity and instructions with a model client, then connects the tools, capabilities, and runtime components that the assistant can use.
text: Agent Agent is the coordinator for one configured assistant. It combines identity and instructions with a model client, then connects the tools, capabilities, and runtime components that the assistant can use. On each run, Agent prepares the prompt, calls the reasoning loop, routes tool calls, and returns the response and updated context. You can add memory, knowledge, skills, middleware, output rules, a workspace, and an executor as the application needs them.

title: Run lifecycle and event stream
summary: run_stream_events() is the low-level interface for one agent turn. It accepts a task and optional conversation context, then yields lifecycle events as they happen and an AgentResponse at the end. Use it when y
text: Run lifecycle and event stream # run_stream_events() is the low-level interface for one agent turn. It accepts a task and optional conversation context, then yields lifecycle events as they happen and an AgentResponse at the end. Use it when your application needs to show progress, inspect tool activity, or decide how to handle a paused run. Agent.run_stream_events async def run_stream_events( self, task: str | CoreMessage | list[CoreMessage] | None = None, run_context: RunContext | None = None, cancellation_token: CancellationToken | None = None, stream_tokens: bool = False, **kwargs: Any, ) -> AsyncGenerator[CoreEvent | AgentResponse, None]: The stream ends with an AgentResponse ; preceding items are CoreEvent instances. This example keeps a stable user/session identity and prints event types while the run is active. Consume one session's event stream from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.core.event_type import CoreEvent from max_ai.types.agent_response import AgentResponse from max_ai.types.run_context import RunContext context = RunContext(user_id="user_001", session_id="support_session") response: AgentResponse | None = None async with agent: async for item in agent.run_stream_events( task="Summarize the open support request.", run_context=context, stream_tokens=True, ): if isinstance(item, AgentResponse): response = item elif isinstance(item, CoreEvent): print(item.event_type) if response is not None: print(response.final_text) print(response.finish_reason) Arguments Argument Purpose task A text task, one CoreMessage , a list of messages, or None . This is the new input for the turn; pass messages when you need a non-text or prebuilt conversation input. run_context The RunContext holding user/session IDs, conversation messages, tool state, and runtime state. Reuse it to continue a conversation; if omitted, Agent creates a fresh context. cancellation_token An optional CancellationToken linked to the run. Trigger it when the caller needs to stop an active turn. stream_tokens When True , the stream includes model token-chunk events as they arrive. Keep it False when only lifecycle and tool events are needed. kwargs Additional keyword arguments forwarded to the configured reasoning loop. Use these for loop-specific options. Events and final response CoreEvent items describe activity such as a task starting, a reasoning step, a tool call, a model chunk, or a pause. Read event_type to identify the event and inspect its fields for details. The final AgentResponse includes final_text , finish_reason , usage, and the updated context . If a response needs approval or user input, resolve the pending item in its context before resuming. The application should collect the user's decision; do not start a new task with unresolved tool calls. Resolve an approval and continue context = RunContext(user_id="user_001", session_id="support_session") async with agent: response = await agent.run( "Send the prepared email?", run_context=context, ) if response.needs_approval and response.context is not None: pending = response.pending_approvals[0] approved_by_user = input("Approve this action? [y/N] ").lower() == "y" response.context.tool_state.apply_approval( pending.id, approved=approved_by_user, ) response = await agent.resume(run_context=response.context) For a pending question, use response.context.tool_state.apply_user_answer(record.id, answer) and then call agent.resume(run_context=response.context) . Resume uses the same conversation and does not add a new task. Other run methods and cleanup Method Use it when run() You want one final AgentResponse without consuming intermediate events. run_stream() You want assistant text chunks as they arrive. run_stream_events() You want typed lifecycle events and the final response in one stream. resume() You have resolved a pending approval or question and want the same turn to continue. Use async with agent so the Agent closes managed execution sessions and MCP connections when the scope ends. The default local executor runs on the host; use Docker or Modal when you need an isolated execution environment. See the Executor guide .

title: ComponentBase contract
summary: The shared Python class is ComponentBase[ConfigT] . It provides component identity and serialization hooks for a typed configuration. It is not an abstract class, so these hooks raise NotImplementedError by def
text: ComponentBase contract # The shared Python class is ComponentBase[ConfigT] . It provides component identity and serialization hooks for a typed configuration. It is not an abstract class, so these hooks raise NotImplementedError by default instead of being enforced with @abstractmethod . Agent-facing contracts such as memory and knowledge inherit through CoreAgentCapabilities , which adds a lifecycle and the shared capability interface. Shared component base class ComponentBase(Generic[ConfigT]): component_type: ClassVar[ComponentType] component_schema: ClassVar[type[BaseModel]] def _to_config(self) -> ConfigT: ... @classmethod def _from_config(cls, config: ConfigT) -> Self: ... class MyComponent(ComponentBase[MyConfig]): component_type = "my_component" component_schema = MyConfig def _to_config(self) -> MyConfig: return MyConfig(path=self.path) @classmethod def _from_config(cls, config: MyConfig) -> "MyComponent": return cls(path=config.path) Methods to override Method Purpose _to_config() Return a Pydantic config containing the data needed to rebuild this component. Keep secrets out; serialize environment variable names instead. _from_config(config) Build a component instance from its validated config. _from_config_past_version(config, version) Optionally migrate older stored configs. Override when a component changes config schema between versions. These config hooks raise NotImplementedError by default; Python does not enforce them with @abstractmethod . CoreLifecycleComponent adds async connection hooks, and CoreAgentCapabilities builds on it for agent-facing registries. The individual BaseComponent pages show each contract declaration and its abstract methods. More in GitHub →

title: Base class and contract methods
summary: This is the provider contract for an LLM client. The base class owns the shared run pipeline; a provider subclass translates messages and tool schemas, normalizes usage, and implements completion and streaming.

The base class owns the shared run pipeline; a provider subclass translates messages and tool schemas, normalizes usage, and implements completion and streaming. CoreChatCompletionClient · complete class API class CoreChatCompletionClient(ComponentBase[BaseModel], ABC): """Abstract base class for all MaxAI chat completion clients.""" API_KEY_ENV: t.ClassVar[str | None] = None def __init__( self, model: str, api_key: str | SecretStr | None = None, config: ModelConfig | None = None, *, api_key_env: str | None = None, **kwargs: t.Any, ) -> None: """Initialize a client instance. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... @staticmethod def _require_type(value: t.Any, expected: type[T], field: str) -> T: """Validate a value against an expected Python type. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... @staticmethod def _resolve_api_key(key: str | SecretStr | None) -> SecretStr | None: """Normalize an API key argument to ``SecretStr | None``. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... async def run( self, ctx: RunContext, prompts: PromptCtx, tools: list["CoreTool"] | None = None, output_format: t.Type[BaseModel] | None = None, stream: bool = False, **kwargs: t.Any, ) -> t.Union[ChatCompletionResult, t.AsyncGenerator[ChatCompletionChunk, None]]: """Execute a chat completion request. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... @abstractmethod def format_messages( self, ctx: "RunContext", prompts: PromptCtx ) -> list[CoreMessage]: """Assemble the full message list for the LLM call. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... @abstractmethod def build_api_messages(self, messages: list[CoreMessage]) -> list[dict[str, t.Any]]: """Convert ``CoreMessage`` instances to the provider's wire format. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... @abstractmethod def build_tool_schema(self, tools: list["CoreTool"]) -> list[dict[str, t.Any]]: """Convert ``CoreTool`` instances to the provider's tool schema. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... @abstractmethod def normalize_usage_stats(self, usage: t.Any) -> Usage: """Normalize the provider's usage payload into framework ``Usage``. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... @abstractmethod async def complete( self, messages: list[dict[str, t.Any]], tools: list[dict[str, t.Any]] | None, output_format: t.Type[BaseModel] | None, **kwargs: t.Any, ) -> ChatCompletionResult: """Execute a single (non-streaming) chat completion call. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... @abstractmethod async def stream( self, messages: list[dict[str, t.Any]], tools: list[dict[str, t.Any]] | None, output_format: t.Type[BaseModel] | None, **kwargs: t.Any, ) -> t.AsyncGenerator[ChatCompletionChunk, None]: """Execute a streaming chat completion call. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... Method What it receives or returns format_messages() Receives the run context and rendered prompt layers; returns framework messages in provider order. build_api_messages() Receives framework messages; converts them to the provider request format. build_tool_schema() Receives CoreTool objects; returns provider-native tool definitions. normalize_usage_stats() Receives the provider usage payload; returns Max AI Usage. complete() Receives provider messages, tools, and output format; returns a normalized ChatCompletionResult. stream() Receives the same request data; yields normalized ChatCompletionChunk objects.

title: Base class and contract methods
summary: This base class implements the common compaction flow and calls one strategy hook. A subclass supplies the policy for reducing older conversation groups within the token budget.
text: Base class and contract methods # This base class implements the common compaction flow and calls one strategy hook. A subclass supplies the policy for reducing older conversation groups within the token budget. CoreCompaction · complete class API class CoreCompaction(ComponentBase[CompactionConfig], ABC): """Base for strategies that keep a run within its context window.""" component_type = "compaction" component_schema = CompactionConfig def __init__( self, *, threshold: float = 0.8, keep_ratio: float = 0.4, min_keep_groups: int = 2, truncate_tool_outputs: bool = True, tool_output_max_tokens: int = 500, drop_harness_messages: bool = True, update_memory: bool = True, memory_max_tokens: int = 1000, client: CoreChatCompletionClient | None = None, token_counter: TokenCounter | None = None, ) -> None: # Validated through the config so bad values fail at construction. """Initialize the compaction strategy and its shared runtime options. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def should_compact( self, ctx: RunContext, prompts: PromptCtx, max_context_tokens: int, max_output_tokens: int, ) -> bool: """Cheap check the loop runs before every model call. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... async def compact( self, *, ctx: RunContext, prompts: PromptCtx, max_context_tokens: int, client: CoreChatCompletionClient, memory: CoreMemoryRegistry | None = None, ) -> CompactionResult: """Run the full pipeline. Never mutates ``ctx``. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... @abstractmethod async def _compact( self, blocks: list[MessageGroup], *, state: dict[str, JsonValue], budget_tokens: int, client: CoreChatCompletionClient, ) -> CompactionResult: """Strategy hook. Receives whole blocks only, so it cannot split a tool call from its results. Returns the new window in ``messages``, what left it in ``old_messages`` and its new ``state``. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... def _over_limit( self, blocks: list[MessageGroup], *, live_tokens: int, threshold: int, ) -> bool: """Whether the window needs compacting. Asked before compacting and again after the prune pass (if pruning was enough, ``_compact`` is skipped). Default: live tokens (history included) over the threshold; ``threshold`` is 0 when the model window is unknown. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def render(self, state: dict[str, JsonValue]) -> str | None: """What the model sees of the compacted past (a system prompt block). Default: nothing. Summary strategies return their summary. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def _prune( self, blocks: list[MessageGroup], *, current_turn_start: int, ) -> list[MessageGroup]: """Cheap, LLM-free cleanup of blocks older than the ``min_keep_groups`` newest. Returns NEW blocks; never edits the original messages. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def _shrink(self, message: CoreMessage) -> CoreMessage: """Copy of ``message`` with oversized tool output/arguments cut down. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def _truncate_text(self, text: str, cap: int) -> str | None: """First ``cap`` tokens of ``text`` plus its original size, or ``None`` when it already fits. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... async def _update_memory( self, old_messages: list[CoreMessage], *, memory: CoreMemoryRegistry, client: CoreChatCompletionClient, ) -> None: """Save durable facts from messages leaving the window. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def _transcript(self, messages: list[CoreMessage], cap: int) -> str: """``[role/source] text`` per message, each cut to ``cap`` tokens. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... async def _ask( self, client: CoreChatCompletionClient, task: str, output_format: type[OutputT], max_tokens: int, ) -> OutputT | str: """One structured request with no tools. Returns the parsed model; JSON cut by ``max_tokens`` keeps its complete fields; anything else comes back as the raw text. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def _validate(self, messages: list[CoreMessage]) -> None: """Check the window a provider will accept, or raise ``CompactionError``. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def _to_config(self) -> CompactionConfig: """Return the serializable settings for this compaction strategy. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... @classmethod def _from_config(cls, config: CompactionConfig) -> t.Self: """Build a compaction strategy from its validated configuration. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... Method What it receives or returns _compact() Receives complete message groups, strategy state, a token budget, and the model client. Returns a CompactionResult with retained messages, archived messages, and updated state.

title: Base class and contract methods

text: Base class and contract methods # This is the execution provider contract. An executor creates and manages an ExecutionSession and runs tools or commands inside that session. The base class defines the operations; a concrete executor decides where they run. ExecutorBase · complete class API class ExecutorBase(ComponentBase[BaseModel], ABC): """Implement once per provider: Local, Docker, Modal.""" component_type = "executor" @abstractmethod async def run_tool( self, session: ExecutionSession, tool, record, context, cancellation_token: CancellationToken | None = None, ): """Invoke a native CoreTool in this provider; never fall back to host. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... @abstractmethod async def execute( self, session: ExecutionSession, command: str, *, timeout: float = 60, cancellation_token: CancellationToken | None = None, ) -> ExecutionResult: """Run Bash; timeout/cancellation must terminate its owned processes. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... @abstractmethod async def execute_argv( self, session: ExecutionSession, argv: list[str], *, stdin: str | None = None, timeout: float = 60, cancellation_token: CancellationToken | None = None, ) -> ExecutionResult: """Execute an argument vector without shell interpolation, with bounded output. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... @abstractmethod async def connect( self, workspace: WorkspaceBase, user_id: str, conversation_id: str, ) -> ExecutionSession: """Create/attach a session and mount or expose the user's workspace. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... async def sync(self, session: ExecutionSession, direction: SyncDirection) -> None: """Transfer changed files; shared mounts/no remote copy: no-op by default. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... @abstractmethod async def disconnect(self, session: ExecutionSession) -> None: """Release connections/resources after sync, preserving workspace files. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... @abstractmethod async def clean(self, session: ExecutionSession) -> None: """Idempotently destroy temporary runtime resources, not workspace files. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... @abstractmethod async def rebuild(self, session: ExecutionSession) -> ExecutionSession: """Recreate the runtime with the same workspace identity, not its image. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def _build_environment(self) -> Environment: """Build a Jinja2 Environment. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... @abstractmethod def _default_template(self) -> str: """Subclasses provide their own default template. A concrete subclass must implement this method.""" ... def _resolve_template(self) -> str: # Priority: inline user template > external file > subclass default """Choose and load the template used by this layer. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... @staticmethod def _load_file(file_path: str | Path) -> str: """Read a prompt template from a filesystem path. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... @property def template(self) -> str: """Resolved template source string (read-only). The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def _parse_placeholders(self, template: str) -> frozenset[str]: """Extract all undeclared variables referenced in the template via Jinja's AST. Loop locals (`item` in `{% for item in items %}`) and `{% set %}` locals are excluded — only caller-provided vars remain. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def _required_variables(self) -> set[str]: """Variables that MUST be supplied to render(). The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def _optional_variables(self) -> set[str]: """Variables that MAY be supplied to render(). The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def validate_placeholders(self) -> None: """Verify template variables match the declared contract. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... @classmethod def _from_config(cls, config: StackConfig) -> t.Self: """Build a prompt layer from its validated configuration. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def render(self, variables: t.Mapping[str, t.Any]) -> str: """Render the compiled template with the given variables. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... def __repr__(self) -> str: """Return a readable representation of this prompt layer. The base class provides this behavior; override it only to customize it.""" ... Method What it receives or returns _default_template() Returns the Jinja2 template text. title: The contract catalog
text: The contract catalog # Model CoreChatCompletionClient A provider-neutral call/stream interface for messages, prompts, tools, and usage. Prompt CoreLayer A Jinja2-backed layer with declared variables and serializable template configuration. Tools CoreTool A tool name, description, JSON Schema parameters, approval mode, and async execute method. Reason BaseReasoning A per-run bound loop; ReAct supplies the default iterative implementation. Close CompletionBase A gate that observes a turn and decides whether the proposed final answer may close it. Context CoreMemoryRegistry , CoreSkillBase , CoreKnowledgeRegistry Distinct contracts for personal memory, packaged procedures, and on-demand retrieval. Runtime WorkspaceBase , ExecutorBase Separate persistent user files from execution of runtime tools. Control CoreCompaction , CoreMiddleware Manage long conversations and intercept run/model/tool lifecycle hooks. Stores CoreContextRegistry , session and quota stores Additional storage contracts; context registries are available independently of the current Agent constructor. Component ComponentBase Defines provider identity and config serialization/deserialization for trusted components.

title: Reasoning and middleware contracts
summary: These contracts receive different parts of a run. Reasoning drives the loop; middleware observes or changes selected lifecycle events.
text: Reasoning and middleware contracts # These contracts receive different parts of a run. Reasoning drives the loop; middleware observes or changes selected lifecycle events. BaseReasoning : the loop and its inputs Receives: RunContext (messages, tool records, and run state), a rendered PromptCtx , per-run BaseLoopState , and optional streaming, cancellation, output-format, and evaluation settings. The Agent binds runtime dependencies such as the client, dispatcher, middleware chain, compaction strategy, and memory when a run starts. Returns: An async stream of CoreEvent objects. A custom loop records assistant and tool messages in the context, registers tool calls before dispatch, and emits a completion event when the turn ends. Reasoning loop contract async def execute_reasoning_loop( self, ctx: RunContext, prompts: PromptCtx, loop_state: BaseLoopState, stream_tokens: bool = False, cancellation_token: CancellationToken | None = None, output_format: type[BaseModel] | None = None, eval_criteria: list[str] | None = None, **kwargs: Any, ) -> AsyncGenerator[CoreEvent, None]: ... The default implementation is ReactLoop . Use Agent(reasoning=...) to select a strategy; keep per-run mutable state in the bound loop state or RunContext , not on the reusable strategy object. CoreMiddleware : run, model, and tool hooks Receives: Each hook gets a MiddlewareContext with the current RunContext , agent name, event emitter, and a per-run state helper. The second argument depends on the hook: a task at run start, a ModelRequest before a model call, or a ToolRequest before an approved tool call. Can return: Model hooks may edit requests or responses; returning a replacement ToolResult from on_tool_request skips that tool execution. The default methods do nothing, so a subclass only needs the hooks it uses. A small run-start middleware from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.base.middleware import CoreMiddleware class RunLogMiddleware(CoreMiddleware): async def on_run_start(self, mw, task): kind = "new run" if task is not None else "resumed run" print(f"{mw.agent}: {kind}") agent = Agent(..., middlewares=[RunLogMiddleware()]) Use mw.state(self) for state that must survive pause and resume. Middleware receives hooks; a completion gate makes the separate decision to accept or reject a final answer.

title: Base contracts, explained
summary: Everything in max_ai.base defines the interfaces that framework components follow. The examples below show what each contract owns and how it is connected to an Agent.
text: Base contracts, explained # Everything in max_ai.base defines the interfaces that framework components follow. The examples below show what each contract owns and how it is connected to an Agent. CoreAgentCapabilities : capability base Receives: A typed configuration schema through its component base. Capability registries can connect to resources during the Agent lifecycle and optionally expose tools. Use it for: The shared base of memory, knowledge, skills, and workspace capabilities. Capability contract class CoreAgentCapabilities(CoreLifecycleComponent[ConfigT], ABC): @property def tools(self) -> list[CoreTool]: return [] CoreChatCompletionClient : model provider Receives: A model name, optional API key or environment variable, and provider configuration. Its run() method receives rendered prompt context and messages, plus optional tools and streaming settings. Returns: Normalized completion results or chunks, independent of provider wire formats. Configure the client contract from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.capabilities.clients.openai import OpenAIChatCompletionClient client = OpenAIChatCompletionClient( model="gpt-5.6-luna", api_key="YOUR_API_KEY", ) agent = Agent(..., client=client) CoreCompaction : conversation history Receives: The conversation, rendered prompts, token limits, and current compaction state. A strategy implements _compact ; shared contract code validates and returns the updated message groups and state. Use it for: Keeping the conversation within a model's context window while preserving useful earlier details. Choose a compaction strategy from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.capabilities.compaction.window import SlidingWindowCompaction agent = Agent(..., compaction=SlidingWindowCompaction( max_turns=10, )) CoreKnowledgeRegistry : searchable reference data Receives: A source name , a description for its search tool, and a query with an optional result limit. Returns: Matching KnowledgeBlock records. The registry exposes search_{name} when tool access is enabled. Connect knowledge to an agent from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.capabilities.knowledge.local import LocalKnowledgeRegistry knowledge = LocalKnowledgeRegistry( name="product_docs", description="Search product documentation.", base_path="./agent-data", ) agent = Agent(..., knowledge=[knowledge]) CoreLayer : prompt content Receives: Declared variables from the Agent and runtime context. Its Jinja2 template renders into prompt text before the client call. Use it for: Adding reusable instructions or context while keeping prompt construction composable. Define a prompt layer class TeamRulesLayer(CoreLayer): def _default_template(self) -> str: return "Follow the team rules for {{ team }}." def _required_variables(self) -> set[str]: return {"team"} CoreMemoryRegistry : user and session memory Receives: A user and session scope from RunContext , plus memory records to create, update, list, or search. Use it for: Information that changes over time and belongs to a particular user or conversation. Attach memory from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.capabilities.memory.local import LocalMemoryRegistry from max_ai.types.run_context import RunContext memory = LocalMemoryRegistry(base_path="./agent-data") agent = Agent(..., memory=memory) context = RunContext(user_id="user_001", session_id="session_001") CoreMiddleware : lifecycle hooks Receives: A middleware context and the event payload for run, model, or tool hooks. Hooks may observe or return an updated request or response. Use it for: Logging, tracing, request changes, or handling tool results around an Agent run. Register middleware from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.base.middleware import CoreMiddleware class RunLogMiddleware(CoreMiddleware): async def on_run_start(self, mw, task): print(mw.agent, "started") agent = Agent(..., middlewares=[RunLogMiddleware()]) CoreSkillBase : reusable procedures Receives: A source location and a list of selected skill names. Preparation loads each skill's SKILL.md and metadata into the registry. Use it for: Giving an Agent task-specific procedures and supporting files that it can consult when needed. Attach skills from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.capabilities.skills.local import LocalSkillRegistry skills = LocalSkillRegistry( source="./skills", skills=["invoice-review"], ) agent = Agent(..., skills=skills) WorkspaceBase : user files Receives: A user ID and optional conversation ID at run time. The workspace prepares directories and downloads or uploads files for local or remote storage. Use it for: Keeping files available between runs for a user, including files used by tools and skills. Attach a workspace from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.capabilities.workspace.local import LocalWorkspace workspace = LocalWorkspace(root="./agent-data") agent = Agent(..., workspace=workspace) For more, see GitHub.

title: Core runtime
summary: The typed state and orchestration inside the harness. These modules explain how a full conversation survives repeated model calls, tool actions, and pauses.
text: Core runtime The typed state and orchestration inside the harness. These modules explain how a full conversation survives repeated model calls, tool actions, and pauses.

title: RunContext: the conversation state
summary: RunContext lives in max_ai.types and is the state passed between turns. It holds user_id , session_id , run_id , live messages, older message history, tool state, plan, compaction state, runtime state, and gate
text: RunContext: the conversation state # RunContext lives in max_ai.types and is the state passed between turns. It holds user_id , session_id , run_id , live messages, older message history, tool state, plan, compaction state, runtime state, and gate evidence. The Agent binds memory and workspace access to its user/session IDs. Two turns in one conversation ctx = RunContext(user_id="u1", session_id="support-42") first = await agent.run("Review this order", run_context=ctx) second = await agent.run("Now summarize the result", run_context=first.context) A new task keeps the conversation messages. Tool calls pending approval must be resolved before adding a new task. Runs in the same user/session are serialized; other sessions can overlap.

title: Sessions: load, run, save
summary: The Agent never touches storage — the host owns the RunContext lifecycle: load it before the turn, run the agent, save the result after. LocalSessionStore ( max_ai.capabilities.session_store ) implements this o
text: Sessions: load, run, save # The Agent never touches storage — the host owns the RunContext lifecycle: load it before the turn, run the agent, save the result after. LocalSessionStore ( max_ai.capabilities.session_store ) implements this on disk; a MongoDB-backed store follows the same CoreSessionStore contract. Host-owned session lifecycle from max_ai.capabilities.session_store import LocalSessionStore store = LocalSessionStore(base_path="./agent-data") ctx = await store.load(user_id, session_id) or RunContext(user_id=user_id, session_id=session_id) response = await agent.run(text, run_context=ctx) await store.save(response.context) This keeps the Agent stateless and reusable across requests: any process can load a saved RunContext , continue the conversation, and save it back, which is what lets one Agent instance serve many users concurrently.

title: Messages, tool state, and events
text: Messages, tool state, and events # Messages core.messages Typed user, assistant, system, and tool messages; text, image, audio, and file parts. Tools core.tool Registry, dispatcher, and state for call validation, routing, approvals, and results. Events core.event_type + events_bus Observable model, tool, completion, input, and approval activity. Runtime environment + executor Manage execution sessions and references to local or remote tools.

title: Embeddings and retrieval
summary: CoreEmbedding ( max_ai.base.embedding ) turns text into vectors, in batches and with a cache, so memory and knowledge backends can search by meaning instead of exact text, in any language. It is infrastructure
text: Embeddings and retrieval # CoreEmbedding ( max_ai.base.embedding ) turns text into vectors, in batches and with a cache, so memory and knowledge backends can search by meaning instead of exact text, in any language. It is infrastructure passed to a registry's embedding= argument, not an Agent constructor input. Local FastEmbedEmbedding Runs a small multilingual model on-device. pip install "maxai[embeddings]" . The default when knowledge search needs one. API OpenAIEmbedding No model download — better for serverless deployments. Same CoreEmbedding contract. Knowledge search uses one by default (local); memory only embeds when given one explicitly. The SQLite and MongoDB backends store each vector next to its record, so nothing is re-embedded after a restart — and MongoDBMemoryRegistry / MongoDBKnowledgeRegistry use MongoDB's native $vectorSearch when the server supports it (Atlas, or the mongodb/mongodb-atlas-local image), falling back to ranking in Python otherwise. Memory that searches by meaning from max_ai.capabilities.memory.local import LocalMemoryRegistry from max_ai.core.embeddings import FastEmbedEmbedding memory = LocalMemoryRegistry(base_path="./agent-data", embedding=FastEmbedEmbedding()) # search_memory now matches paraphrases and other languages, not just substrings.

Budget core.compaction Message grouping, token counting, and context-window budgeting. Policy core.middleware + core.runtime Middleware chain and runtime status calculations. title: Capabilities
summary: The public Agent composes model, reasoning, tool, execution, and optional context providers. Each provider implements a contract under max_ai.base and ships concrete implementations under max_ai.capabilities .
text: Capabilities The public Agent composes model, reasoning, tool, execution, and optional context providers. Each provider implements a contract under max_ai.base and ships concrete implementations under max_ai.capabilities .

title: Workspace and execution
summary: WorkspaceBase owns persistent user files and skill materialization. ExecutorBase runs executor-routed tools, and EnvironmentManager manages sessions linking the two. The Agent defaults to LocalWorkspace and Loc
text: Workspace and execution # WorkspaceBase owns persistent user files and skill materialization. ExecutorBase runs executor-routed tools, and EnvironmentManager manages sessions linking the two. The Agent defaults to LocalWorkspace and LocalExecutor ; Docker and Modal are alternatives for execution. Local execution runs on the host and is not a sandbox. Workspace and executor are separate providers. WorkspaceBase EnvironmentManager ExecutorBase Remote workspaces AzureBlobWorkspace and MinIOWorkspace ( max_ai.capabilities.workspace ) keep a user's files in object storage instead of local disk, so a serverless instance or another server sees the same workspace. The Agent downloads a user's files when a run starts and uploads changes when it ends; only a manifest of file hashes is compared, so unchanged files never move. Scratchpads and materialized skills stay local, since they are throwaway per run. Object-storage workspace from max_ai.capabilities.workspace import AzureBlobWorkspace, MinIOWorkspace workspace = AzureBlobWorkspace( "https://myaccount.blob.core.windows.net/workspaces", api_key_env="AZURE_STORAGE_KEY", ) # Or: MinIOWorkspace("http://localhost:9000", bucket="workspaces", # access_key_env="MINIO_ACCESS_KEY", secret_key_env="MINIO_SECRET_KEY") agent = Agent(..., workspace=workspace) Needs pip install "maxai[azure-blob]" or "maxai[minio]" . MinIO's endpoint also accepts any S3-compatible store, including AWS S3.

title: Memory
summary: These are three different ways to add context. Memory is user/session data that can change during a run. A skill is a reusable procedure with instructions and files. Knowledge is a curated collection searched o
text: Memory # These are three different ways to add context. Memory is user/session data that can change during a run. A skill is a reusable procedure with instructions and files. Knowledge is a curated collection searched on demand. Enable each by passing its registry to Agent ; a configured capability contributes its tools and prompt layer. Memory personal · session scoped ↔ Agent run RunContext user_id + session_id ↔ Skills instructions · workspace files Knowledge curated source · retrieval tool → Model context layer text + tool results ← SKILL.md read when the task calls for it Choose a backend based on where the agent runs: Local for a simple file store, SQLite for a shared local database, or MongoDB for state shared across application servers. Each registry accepts the same user and session scope from the Agent. Local memory Receives: base_path is required. You can also set tool_mode , context_days , and an embedding . The Agent binds each run's user_id and session_id . Stores: A JSON file for each user and session under base_path/memory/ . Best for a single process and simple local persistence. Search: Cross-session memory search defaults to local semantic embeddings. Set embedding=None to use word matching. Local registry LocalMemoryRegistry( base_path="./agent-data", tool_mode=MemoryToolMode.FULL, context_days=30, ) SQLite memory Receives: Required base_path ; optional db_name (default memory.sqlite3 ), tool_mode , context_days , search_limit , and embedding . Stores: Memory records and their embeddings in one SQLite file, scoped by user, session, and category. Suitable for one process or a small deployment on one machine. Search: Semantic search is the default. Passing embedding=None uses text matching instead. SQLite registry SQLiteMemoryRegistry( base_path="./agent-data", db_name="memory.sqlite3", search_limit=20, ) MongoDB memory Receives: Optional database , collection , uri_env , server_selection_timeout_ms , context_days , search_limit , and embedding . The MongoDB URI is read from the named environment variable. Stores: User and session records in a shared MongoDB collection, so multiple application servers can use the same store. Install the mongodb extra. Search: Semantic search is the default. MongoDB Atlas can use vector search; other servers rank candidates in Python. Pass embedding=None for text matching. MongoDB registry MongoDBMemoryRegistry( uri_env="MONGODB_URI", database="max_ai", collection="memory", )

title: Skills: local procedures
summary: A local skill source contains one directory per selected skill, each with a SKILL.md . Its YAML frontmatter declares name and description . During preparation the registry validates selected skills and reads th
text: Skills: local procedures # A local skill source contains one directory per selected skill, each with a SKILL.md . Its YAML frontmatter declares name and description . During preparation the registry validates selected skills and reads their short catalog entries. SkillsLayer gives the model that catalog; when a task matches, the model uses the built-in read_file tool to open the full SKILL.md , then follows its procedure and uses any accompanying scripts or references. Skills are not callable tools: they teach the agent when and how to use tools. Example skill package and Agent wiring skills/ └── invoice-review/ ├── SKILL.md # YAML name/description + procedure ├── references/ # optional detailed guidance └── scripts/ # optional helper programs from max_ai.capabilities.skills.local import LocalSkillRegistry skills = LocalSkillRegistry(source="./skills", skills=["invoice-review"]) # Pass skills=skills and workspace=LocalWorkspace(...) to Agent. Preparation stages selected skills in the registry cache. Before a run, the workspace materializes them under its per-user skills/ directory; existing workspace edits are preserved.

title: Knowledge: retrieval on demand
summary: A knowledge registry turns a curated document collection into a named search tool. Choose Local, SQLite, or MongoDB for storage; each backend below explains its constructor inputs, ingestion, and search behavio
text: Knowledge: retrieval on demand # A knowledge registry turns a curated document collection into a named search tool. Choose Local, SQLite, or MongoDB for storage; each backend below explains its constructor inputs, ingestion, and search behavior. capabilities/memory capabilities/skills capabilities/knowledge context registry exists separately; not an Agent constructor input Local knowledge Receives: Required name , description , and base_path ; optional tool_mode and embedding . The name determines the search tool, such as search_product_docs . Stores: Reads blocks from base_path/knowledge/{name}.json . Document ingestion is external to the Agent; prepare the JSON file before searching. Search: The model supplies a query and optional result limit. The default local embedding ranks matching KnowledgeBlock records by meaning. Local knowledge source LocalKnowledgeRegistry( name="product_docs", description="Search product manuals.", base_path="./agent-data", ) SQLite knowledge Receives: Required name , description , and base_path ; optional db_name , tool_mode , min_score , and embedding . Stores: Each block's text, metadata, and embedding in SQLite. Use upsert_block(block_id, block) and delete_block(block_id) from application code to manage documents. Search: The Agent exposes a named search tool. New or changed block text is embedded on write; the query is embedded when searched. SQLite knowledge source SQLiteKnowledgeRegistry( name="product_docs", description="Search product manuals.", base_path="./agent-data", min_score=0.2, ) MongoDB knowledge Receives: Required name and description ; optional database , collection , uri_env , server_selection_timeout_ms , tool_mode , min_score , and embedding . The connection URI is read from the named environment variable. Stores: Knowledge blocks in a shared MongoDB collection. Use the registry's upsert/delete methods from application code to manage the source. Install the mongodb extra. Search: By default, embeddings enable semantic retrieval and Atlas vector search where supported. Set embedding=None to use MongoDB text search. MongoDB knowledge source MongoDBKnowledgeRegistry( name="product_docs", description="Search product manuals.", uri_env="MONGODB_URI", database="max_ai", collection="knowledge", )

title: Model providers
summary: CoreChatCompletionClient is the framework contract. A provider adapter maps typed messages, tool schemas, structured output, streaming chunks, and usage data to that provider's API and maps responses back. The
text: Model providers # CoreChatCompletionClient is the framework contract. A provider adapter maps typed messages, tool schemas, structured output, streaming chunks, and usage data to that provider's API and maps responses back. The reasoning loop depends on this contract, so it does not need provider-specific branches. Local Ollama Local model server; configure model and host, with optional thinking and generation options. Useful for local development and deployments where the Ollama service is managed by you. API OpenAI OpenAI chat-completions client. Configure model and API-key environment variable; optional base URL, organization, project, and request options. Gateway OpenRouter OpenAI-compatible routing through OpenRouter, with routing/fallback options and provider-specific settings. The client carries a ModelConfig describing context window, output limit, tool calling, vision/audio, thinking, and tokenizer support. These are capability declarations consumed by runtime features such as compaction and multimodal message handling; choose values that match the actual model. Output is capped at 32K tokens across every client — room for a whole file in one tool call — and a reply cut at the limit is explained back to the model instead of silently dropped. Keep API keys in environment variables—serialized client config stores the variable name, not the secret. OpenAI provider setup from max_ai.capabilities.clients.openai import OpenAIChatCompletionClient from max_ai.core.model.llm import ModelConfig # Export OPENAI_API_KEY in the process environment before construction. client = OpenAIChatCompletionClient( model="YOUR_PROVIDER_MODEL", api_key_env="OPENAI_API_KEY", config=ModelConfig(supports_function_calling=True), ) # Pass client=client to Agent. capabilities/clients/ollama capabilities/clients/openai capabilities/clients/openrouter Provider configuration: what the client receives Every provider client needs a provider-specific model . OpenAI accepts an API key or an api_key_env name plus optional base_url , organization , project , ModelConfig , and generation options. OpenRouter adds fallback models and routing preferences. Ollama accepts a host, optional API key, thinking settings, and keep-alive value. ModelConfig declares runtime capabilities such as context window, output limit, tool calling, vision, audio, thinking, and token counting. Choose values that match the model; compaction and message handling rely on them. API credentials can be passed directly, but an environment variable name is safer and is what serialized configuration stores. OpenAI client OpenAIChatCompletionClient( model="YOUR_PROVIDER_MODEL", api_key_env="OPENAI_API_KEY", config=ModelConfig(supports_function_calling=True), )

title: Reasoning · ReAct
summary: BaseReasoning is the loop contract and ReactLoop is the default. Each run binds its own strategy to the model client, tool dispatcher, middleware, and completion bus. Model requests, tool observations, guards,
text: Reasoning · ReAct # BaseReasoning is the loop contract and ReactLoop is the default. Each run binds its own strategy to the model client, tool dispatcher, middleware, and completion bus. Model requests, tool observations, guards, and final responses repeat until the turn closes or pauses. Explore the loop → Reasoning configuration: loop settings and per-run inputs ReactLoop constructor settings are max_loop_iterations (or None to follow the framework setting), max_connection_retries , and guards . The default guards retry schema errors, steer repeated calls, and check the run budget; pass an empty list to disable them. When a run begins, the Agent binds a copy of the reasoning loop to that run's model client, tool dispatcher, middleware chain, compaction strategy, memory, and context limit. The loop method then receives messages and state through RunContext , the prepared prompt, streaming/cancellation settings, and any output schema. Select a loop reasoning = ReactLoop( max_loop_iterations=12, max_connection_retries=3, ) agent = Agent(..., reasoning=reasoning)

title: Compaction
summary: There is no default: pass compaction=None (or omit it) and the window is never compacted, which is fine for short sessions. Use SlidingWindowCompaction to drop the oldest turns without an LLM call, or SummaryCo
text: Compaction # There is no default: pass compaction=None (or omit it) and the window is never compacted, which is fine for short sessions. Use SlidingWindowCompaction to drop the oldest turns without an LLM call, or SummaryCompaction(threshold=0.8, keep_ratio=0.4) to summarize older turns with the model once the window is 80% full, keeping the summary in the prompt. Pass a strategy as compaction=... ; it runs inside the loop before model calls. Its summary and counters live with the conversation RunContext ; compaction reduces model context, not the need to persist the conversation. SlidingWindowCompaction SummaryCompaction RunContext.compaction_state Compaction configuration: token budget and strategy Compaction is opt-in. The shared strategy settings include threshold (the fraction of the model window that triggers compaction), keep_ratio , min_keep_groups , tool-output truncation controls, and whether extracted older facts update memory. SlidingWindowCompaction also receives max_turns and removes old turns without an LLM summary. SummaryCompaction receives summary_max_tokens and message_cap_tokens ; it uses the model client to summarize older turns. Both return updated messages and state to the reasoning loop. Choose a strategy compaction = SummaryCompaction( threshold=0.8, keep_ratio=0.4, summary_max_tokens=2000, ) agent = Agent(..., compaction=compaction)

title: Completion gates
summary: RuntimeCompletionGate is included in every Agent. It checks whether an answer is ready to close: open plans, declared Bash outputs, and unresolved failures can keep work in the loop. Pass additional CompletionB
text: Completion gates # RuntimeCompletionGate is included in every Agent. It checks whether an answer is ready to close: open plans, declared Bash outputs, and unresolved failures can keep work in the loop. Pass additional CompletionBase implementations through gates=[...] . A gate's on_final_response(ctx) decision can accept, reject, or wait; observation hooks may record evidence but do not veto closure. Configure built-in checks with RuntimeCompletionGate(RuntimeGateConfig(...)) in gates . See gate outcomes →

title: Middleware
summary: CoreMiddleware hooks surround the run ( on_run_start , on_final_response , on_run_end , on_run_error ), every model call ( on_model_request , on_model_chunk , on_model_response , on_model_error ), and every app
text: Middleware # CoreMiddleware hooks surround the run ( on_run_start , on_final_response , on_run_end , on_run_error ), every model call ( on_model_request , on_model_chunk , on_model_response , on_model_error ), and every approved tool call ( on_tool_request , on_tool_response ). Raising StopRun(message) from a run or model hook ends the turn cleanly; a tool hook blocks a single call by returning a ToolResult instead. Pass middleware through middlewares=[...] ; middleware observes and controls runtime behavior, while gates decide completion. LoggingMiddleware BudgetMiddleware TracingMiddleware Budget and quotas BudgetMiddleware enforces two kinds of limits at once: per-task caps ( max_tokens , max_cost_usd , max_seconds ) that stop a single run, and per-user quotas ( quota=QuotaLimits(...) ) that track daily and monthly spend across runs in a quota_store . LocalQuotaStore keeps counters on disk for a single process; MongoDBQuotaStore shares them across servers. Per-task limits and a daily quota from max_ai.capabilities.middleware import BudgetMiddleware from max_ai.capabilities.quota_store import LocalQuotaStore from max_ai.core.model.quota import QuotaLimits budget = BudgetMiddleware( max_tokens=200_000, max_cost_usd=2.0, max_seconds=120, quota=QuotaLimits(daily_cost_usd=20.0, monthly_cost_usd=300.0), quota_store=LocalQuotaStore(base_path="./agent-data"), ) agent = Agent(..., middlewares=[budget]) Tracing TracingMiddleware() emits OpenTelemetry spans for runs, model calls, and tool calls. Call configure_langfuse() once at startup to send those spans to a Langfuse instance — docker-infra/ ships a local one for development. Middleware configuration: hooks and their inputs Each hook receives a MiddlewareContext (the current run, agent name, event emitter, and per-run state) plus the object for that lifecycle point: a task, a ModelRequest , a model result/chunk, or a ToolRequest / ToolResult . Run and model hooks can observe or change requests and responses. Returning a ToolResult from on_tool_request supplies the tool result without executing the tool. Use middlewares=[...] on Agent. BudgetMiddleware receives per-run token/cost/time/call limits and optional quota/store settings; TracingMiddleware receives content-capture settings and an optional tracer provider. Attach a middleware budget = BudgetMiddleware( max_tokens=100_000, max_seconds=90, ) agent = Agent(..., middlewares=[budget])

title: Prompt layers
summary: Prompt layers turn agent configuration and optional registry data into model instructions. They are rendered for each run, then adapted to the selected provider's message format.
text: Prompt layers Prompt layers turn agent configuration and optional registry data into model instructions. They are rendered for each run, then adapted to the selected provider's message format.

title: From values to prompt
summary: The user task and tool schemas remain separate inputs. The diagram follows only the prompt instructions from configuration to the provider request.
text: From values to prompt # The user task and tool schemas remain separate inputs. The diagram follows only the prompt instructions from configuration to the provider request. 01 · Collect Agent + registries Read identity fields and collect configured skills, knowledge tool names, and memory context. Agent._prompt_variables() → 02 · Render Ordered templates Each active CoreLayer receives the shared values and renders its own Jinja2 template. layer.render(variables) → 03 · Package PromptCtx Rendered text is stored by layer class in rendered_layers , with the source stack and values. Agent._prompts() → 04 · Inject Model client The reasoning loop passes PromptCtx to client.run() ; the client builds provider-native messages. client.format_messages()

title: The prompt stack
summary: max_ai.agents.Agent._build_prompt_stack() creates the prompt layers in this order. Policy, task analysis, rendering, and session state are always present. Skills, knowledge, and memory layers appear only when t
text: The prompt stack # max_ai.agents.Agent._build_prompt_stack() creates the prompt layers in this order. Policy, task analysis, rendering, and session state are always present. Skills, knowledge, and memory layers appear only when their matching registries are passed to the agent. 01 AgentPolicyLayer Agent identity, description, developer instructions, and behavior policy. Always · agent fields 02 TaskAnalysisLayer Static guidance for interpreting the task, checking missing information, and deciding whether to plan or clarify. Always · static template 03 RenderingLayer Static response-format guidance for readable text, code, lists, links, and diagrams. Always · static template 04 SkillsLayer Renders available skill names and summaries after the skill registry is prepared. Full instructions stay in the materialized skill package. When skills is set 05 KnowledgeLayer Lets the model know which retrieval tools exist. Search results arrive later as tool-result messages. When knowledge is set 06 MemoryLayer Adds the current memory snapshot and describes available memory operations. When memory is set 07 SessionStateLayer Keeps the current plan and any compaction summary in the prompt so they survive transcript compaction. Always · run state

title: Variable sources
summary: The agent collects values before rendering. A layer only reads the names used by its own template; it does not query a registry directly.
text: Variable sources # The agent collects values before rendering. A layer only reads the names used by its own template; it does not query a registry directly. Template Variables Source AgentPolicyLayer name , description , instructions Agent constructor SkillsLayer loaded_skills skills.get_skills() during prepare KnowledgeLayer retrieval_tools Tool names from knowledge registries MemoryLayer persistent_memories , memory_tools Scoped memory registry TaskAnalysisLayer — Static template text; no run variables RenderingLayer — Static template text; no run variables SessionStateLayer compaction_summary , current_plan RunContext plan and compaction state Not part of the prompt layers The user task and chat history are CoreMessage entries in RunContext . Tool schemas are sent as the separate tools argument to the model client. Knowledge results are added as tool-result messages after retrieval.

title: Rendering a variable
summary: The template declares where a value belongs. At run time CoreLayer.render() inserts values into that position and returns a string. For example, AgentPolicyLayer has this structure:
text: Rendering a variable # The template declares where a value belongs. At run time CoreLayer.render() inserts values into that position and returns a string. For example, AgentPolicyLayer has this structure: Jinja2 template Copy <identity> <name>{{ name }}</name> <description>{{ description }}</description> <instructions>{{ instructions }}</instructions> </identity> Agent values render into the placeholders ↓ Rendered layer text Copy <identity> <name>math-assistant</name> <description>Answers questions with a calculator.</description> <instructions>Use the multiply tool when needed.</instructions> </identity> Templates use Jinja2. `CoreLayer` validates required and optional placeholders when it is constructed; strict rendering surfaces missing values instead of silently producing incomplete instructions.

title: Model client injection
summary: The agent packages the ordered stack and its rendered strings in PromptCtx . The reasoning loop passes it into the client on every model call. The provider adapter decides how to form the actual request.
text: Model client injection # The agent packages the ordered stack and its rendered strings in PromptCtx . The reasoning loop passes it into the client on every model call. The provider adapter decides how to form the actual request. Agent._prompts() and BaseReasoning._call_llm() Copy variables = await self._prompt_variables(ctx) prompts = PromptCtx( stack=self._stack, variables=variables, rendered_layers={ type(layer): layer.render(variables) for layer in self._stack }, ) # ReactLoop supplies prompt context and tool schemas separately. result = await self.client.run( ctx=self._model_context(ctx, transient_messages), prompts=prompts, tools=tools, ) For Ollama, non-empty rendered layers are joined with blank lines into a system message. Conversation history and the current task follow as messages. Other model clients can assemble those pieces differently to match their provider APIs.

title: Create a custom layer
summary: Subclass CoreLayer to define a Jinja2 template, its required run variables, and optional static extra_variables . Give a serializable layer a StackConfig schema and a stable importable provider path. The Agent
text: Create a custom layer # Subclass CoreLayer to define a Jinja2 template, its required run variables, and optional static extra_variables . Give a serializable layer a StackConfig schema and a stable importable provider path. The Agent supplies name , description , and instructions as run variables. Contract shape · abbreviated class OrganizationRulesLayer(Component[StackConfig], CoreLayer): component_schema = StackConfig component_type = "prompts" def _default_template(self) -> str: return "Organization: {{ organization_name }}; agent: {{ name }}" def _required_variables(self) -> set[str]: return {"name"} agent = Agent(..., prompt_layers=[OrganizationRulesLayer( extra_variables={"organization_name": "Acme"})]) CoreLayer uses Jinja2 StrictUndefined , so every template variable must be supplied. Keep the class in an importable module; when deserializing a trusted custom provider, allow its package prefix with allow_providers(...) . See the custom prompt layer example →

title: Integrations
summary: Connect external tools, return structured data, and handle approvals using the same agent runtime.
text: Integrations Connect external tools, return structured data, and handle approvals using the same agent runtime.

title: Connect MCP servers
summary: Pass remote server configurations through the Agent's mcp argument, separate from local Python tools in toolset . The agent connects servers, discovers tools, and dispatches calls; its managed MCP sessions clos
text: Connect MCP servers # Pass remote server configurations through the Agent's mcp argument, separate from local Python tools in toolset . The agent connects servers, discovers tools, and dispatches calls; its managed MCP sessions close when the Agent closes. Server configurations are Pydantic models with JSON round-trip helpers. title: A harness around model decisions
summary: Max AI is a framework for building an agent harness: it assembles instructions and tools, asks a model what to do next, executes allowed actions, records evidence, and decides whether the turn can close. Each r
text: A harness around model decisions # Max AI is a framework for building an agent harness: it assembles instructions and tools, asks a model what to do next, executes allowed actions, records evidence, and decides whether the turn can close. Each responsibility has a replaceable contract. Agent + RunContext → Prompt + provider → Model decision → Tool or final answer → Gate + next turn

title: What BaseReasoning and ReAct do
summary: View the message flow diagram or explore the interactive walkthrough to follow each stage.
text: View the message flow diagram or explore the interactive walkthrough to follow each stage. What BaseReasoning and ReAct do # BaseReasoning defines one turn’s loop contract. The Agent constructs a configuration-only strategy once, then binds a per-run copy to the client, dispatcher, tool context, middleware, and completion bus. ReactLoop calls the model, dispatches tool calls, adds tool messages to the transcript, and repeats. Schema, repetition, and budget guards bound the process. 1 Model request Rendered prompt layers, conversation messages, and tool schemas enter the selected client. 2 Action A tool call is validated and routed. A request for approval or user input pauses the turn. 3 Observation The result becomes a tool message. The next model request sees it. 4 Closure A tool-free answer reaches the gates. Incomplete work returns to the loop; accepted work finishes.

title: Why conversations continue
summary: The loop state for a turn is temporary, but RunContext carries the conversation. Reuse the returned context for the next user message. It retains messages, tool state, plan, compaction summary, and pause eviden
text: Why conversations continue # The loop state for a turn is temporary, but RunContext carries the conversation. Reuse the returned context for the next user message. It retains messages, tool state, plan, compaction summary, and pause evidence. An Agent can therefore handle many turns in one conversation and many separate conversations, with same-session calls queued to keep transcript order. Continue the same conversation response = await agent.run("First question", run_context=ctx) response = await agent.run("Follow-up question", run_context=response.context) Memory is a separate persisted capability scoped to user/session; it does not replace the conversation transcript.

title: What a gate decides
summary: The built-in RuntimeCompletionGate checks turn closure: an empty answer, an open plan, declared Bash outputs, and unresolved Bash failures can produce an incomplete or waiting decision. Application gates implem
text: What a gate decides # The built-in RuntimeCompletionGate checks turn closure: an empty answer, an open plan, declared Bash outputs, and unresolved Bash failures can produce an incomplete or waiting decision. Application gates implement CompletionBase.on_final_response(ctx) for domain evidence. Observation hooks may record evidence in ctx.completion_state ; only the final-response decision can veto closure. completed → return incomplete → another iteration waiting → pause cancelled → stop

title: Pause and resume
summary: Approvals and questions are represented in RunContext.tool_state . The response exposes needs_approval , pending_approvals , needs_input , and pending_questions . After your application applies the decision or
text: Pause and resume # Approvals and questions are represented in RunContext.tool_state . The response exposes needs_approval , pending_approvals , needs_input , and pending_questions . After your application applies the decision or answer to the pending tool record, call agent.resume(run_context=response.context) . The loop restores saved metrics and guard state.

title: Configuration versus state

text: Configuration versus state # Agent.serialize() stores component configuration for rebuilding an Agent. It does not itself store the current conversation; persist the RunContext separately if the conversation must survive a process restart. Provider configurations use environment-variable names for credentials rather than secret values. Avoid putting secrets in instructions or other user-controlled configuration fields. Function tools are Python code and cannot be serialized as components.

title: How to read the stream
summary: Agent.run_stream_events() yields typed CoreEvent objects as work happens, then yields one AgentResponse when the run ends. AgentResponse is the final run result, not an event.
text: How to read the stream Agent.run_stream_events() yields typed CoreEvent objects as work happens, then yields one AgentResponse when the run ends. AgentResponse is the final run result, not an event. A model's final-looking text is not necessarily an accepted answer: LastMessageResponseEvent describes a proposed answer, CompletionRejectedEvent means the completion gate wants another attempt, and TaskCompleteEvent means the gate accepted the response. Tool events use the same tool_call_id to connect a request with its approval, progress, and result. ToolCallEvent describes the requested action; ToolCallResponseEvent carries its ToolResult . The result may also appear in the conversation as a ToolMessage . Send runtime activity to your UI from max_ai.types.agent_response import AgentResponse async def stream_to_ui(agent, ui): async for item in agent.run_stream_events( "Summarize the selected document", stream_tokens=True, ): if isinstance(item, AgentResponse): ui.show_answer(item.final_text) else: ui.add_activity(item.event_type, item) The example leaves agent and ui to the application: the agent is already configured, and the UI decides how to display each event.

summary: A host can turn the stream into a small activity feed while the final answer appears when the AgentResponse arrives.
text: Example UI A host can turn the stream into a small activity feed while the final answer appears when the AgentResponse arrives. Agent run Live activity Reasoning step started reasoning_iteration 10:24:10 Model request model_call 10:24:10 Tool requested tool_call · registered tool 10:24:11 Tool finished tool_call_response · result received 10:24:12 Assistant response streaming model_stream_chunk 10:24:13 Answer accepted task_complete 10:24:13 AgentResponse · final_text The selected document summarizes the project status and next steps. This is an illustrative presentation. Your application can show fewer details, expose tool approval controls, or display model chunks as they arrive.

title: Common event fields
summary: Every event inherits these fields from CoreEvent :
text: Common event fields Every event inherits these fields from CoreEvent : Field Meaning source The component that emitted the event. event_type Stable event name, such as tool_call or model_response. event_id Unique identifier for this event. timestamp When the event was created.

title: Tasks
summary: Task boundaries and whether a proposed final answer passed the completion gate.
text: Tasks Task boundaries and whether a proposed final answer passed the completion gate. Event What it expresses Useful data TaskStartEvent task_start Processing of a task begins. Includes the task text. TaskCompleteEvent task_complete The completion gate accepted the final response. Includes the aggregate completion decision. It is not emitted for a pause, error, or exhausted limit. CompletionRejectedEvent completion_rejected The completion gate rejected a proposed final response, so the model can try again. Includes the decision and its reasons.

title: Model
summary: Model request, response, and streaming output activity.
text: Model Model request, response, and streaming output activity. Event What it expresses Useful data ModelCallEvent model_call A request is being sent to a model. Includes the model name, input messages, and rendered prompt token count. ModelResponseEvent model_response A model response has arrived. Includes response text, whether it contains tool calls, and usage when available. ModelStreamChunkEvent model_stream_chunk A partial model output is available during streaming. Includes the text chunk, optional thinking, and whether it is the final chunk.

title: Reasoning
summary: Reasoning loop progress, planning, and interactions that pause for the user.
text: Reasoning Reasoning loop progress, planning, and interactions that pause for the user. Event What it expresses Useful data ReasoningIterationEvent reasoning_iteration A reasoning loop iteration begins. Includes the current iteration and maximum allowed iterations. ReasoningCompleteEvent reasoning_complete The reasoning loop has stopped. Includes its finish reason and number of iterations. LastMessageResponseEvent last_message_response The model proposed a final text response without requesting tools; the completion gate is about to check it. Includes the proposed response. PlanningEvent planning A plan is starting, changing, finishing, failing, or being skipped. Includes the phase and plan when available. UserInputRequestEvent user_input_request The agent is asking the user a question and pausing for an answer. Includes the question, optional choices, and tool call ID used to store the answer.

title: Agent
summary: Agent selection, execution boundaries, and changes to the active context window.
text: Agent Agent selection, execution boundaries, and changes to the active context window. Event What it expresses Useful data AgentSelectionEvent agent_selection An agent was selected to handle work. Includes the selected agent and optional selection reason. AgentExecutionStartEvent agent_execution_start An agent begins execution. Includes the agent name and context size. AgentExecutionCompleteEvent agent_execution_complete An agent finishes execution. Includes the agent name, success status, and produced message count. CompactionEvent compaction Context compaction begins or ends. Includes phase, strategy, token counts, whether the context changed, and at the end the removed messages and summary.

title: Tools and commands
summary: Tool requests, approval, validation, progress, command execution, and workspace file operations.
text: Tools and commands Tool requests, approval, validation, progress, command execution, and workspace file operations. Event What it expresses Useful data ToolCallEvent tool_call A tool call is about to be handled. Includes tool name, parameters, and tool call ID. This describes the request, not its result. ToolApprovalEvent tool_approval A tool needs a user's approval before it can run. Includes the tool, parameters, call ID, and optional approval reason. ToolAutoApprovalEvent tool_auto_approval Policy approved a tool without asking the user. Includes tool name and call ID. ToolValidationEvent tool_validation Tool parameters have been checked. Includes whether they are valid and any validation errors. ToolProgressEvent tool_progress A long-running tool reports progress. Includes a human-readable update, tool name, and call ID. ToolCallResponseEvent tool_call_response Tool execution finished, successfully or with a failure. Carries the ToolResult and originating call ID. This is the tool's runtime outcome. BashStartedEvent bash_started A shell command is about to execute. Includes the command, declared action, description, and call ID. BashFinishedEvent bash_finished A shell command finished. Includes exit code, duration, timeout status, and whether output was truncated. BashFailedEvent bash_failed A shell command failed to start or run. Includes the call ID and failure message. BashCancelledEvent bash_cancelled A shell command was cancelled. Includes the call ID and cancellation reason. FileReadEvent file_read A workspace file was read successfully. Includes its path, workspace root, content hash, and call ID. DirectoryListedEvent directory_listed A workspace directory was listed successfully. Includes its path, workspace root, entry count, and call ID. FileWrittenEvent file_written A workspace file was written or edited successfully. Includes operation, path, workspace root, content hash, and call ID. FilesSearchedEvent files_searched A workspace file or text search finished. Includes search operation, path, match count, truncation status, and call ID. DirectoryCreatedEvent directory_created A workspace directory was created. Includes its path, workspace root, and call ID. FileDeletedEvent file_deleted A workspace file was deleted. Includes its path, workspace root, content hash, and call ID. FileInfoEvent file_info Information about a workspace file or directory was retrieved. Includes the path, workspace root, item type, and call ID.

title: run_cli
summary: Run the agent in your terminal. The CLI handles input, displays responses and thinking, and can save conversations through a session store. Install the optional cli extra to use it.
text: run_cli # Run the agent in your terminal. The CLI handles input, displays responses and thinking, and can save conversations through a session store. Install the optional cli extra to use it. Signature async def run_cli( agent: Agent, *, show_thinking: bool = True, initial_context: RunContext | None = None, store: CoreSessionStore | None = None, user_id: str | None = None, session_id: str | None = None, ) -> None: cli_example.py Copy import asyncio from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.capabilities.clients.openai import OpenAIChatCompletionClient from max_ai.capabilities.session_store import LocalSessionStore from max_ai.cli import run_cli client = OpenAIChatCompletionClient( model="gpt-5.6-luna", api_key="YOUR_API_KEY", ) agent = Agent( name="Assistant", description="A helpful assistant.", instructions="Answer clearly and briefly.", client=client, ) async def main() -> None: async with agent: await run_cli( agent, show_thinking=True, store=LocalSessionStore("./sessions"), user_id="user_001", session_id=None, ) asyncio.run(main()) The CLI displays the active conversation and accepts the next message in the terminal. The CLI is a host for the agent: it does not require a deployed web service. Build your agent once, pass it to run_cli , and use the terminal to test or chat with it.

With LocalSessionStore , the CLI saves after each turn and enables /resume . user_id Identifies whose sessions are saved. Use the same ID when resuming that user's conversations. session_id Optional ID to load a saved session at startup. Install psycopg[binary].""" import asyncio import os import psycopg from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.base.knowledge import CoreKnowledgeRegistry from max_ai.capabilities.clients.openai import OpenAIChatCompletionClient from max_ai.core import KnowledgeBlock class PostgresKnowledge(CoreKnowledgeRegistry): def __init__(self, url: str) -> None: super().__init__(name="office_notes", description="Notes stored in PostgreSQL.") self.url = url self.connection = None async def connect(self) -> None: self.connection = await psycopg.AsyncConnection.connect(self.url) await self.connection.execute( "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS example_knowledge (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, content TEXT)" ) await self.connection.execute( "INSERT INTO example_knowledge VALUES (%s, %s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING", ("note-1", "Office hours are Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM."), ) await self.connection.commit() async def disconnect(self) -> None: await self.connection.close() async def search(self, query: str, limit: int = 5) -> list[KnowledgeBlock]: cursor = await self.connection.execute( "SELECT content FROM example_knowledge WHERE content ILIKE %s LIMIT %s", (f"%{query}%", limit), ) return [KnowledgeBlock(content=row[0]) for row in await cursor.fetchall()] async def main() -> None: knowledge = PostgresKnowledge(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]) agent = Agent( name="Assistant", description="Answer questions using PostgreSQL.", instructions="Search office_notes for questions about office hours.", client=OpenAIChatCompletionClient(model="gpt-5.6-luna", api_key="YOUR_API_KEY"), knowledge=[knowledge], ) async with agent: response = await agent.run("What are the office hours?") print(response.final_text) await knowledge.disconnect() if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main())

Python Copy """Implement CoreSessionStore with an in-memory dictionary.""" import asyncio from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.base.session_store import CoreSessionStore from max_ai.capabilities.clients.openai import OpenAIChatCompletionClient from max_ai.core.model.session import SessionInfo from max_ai.types.run_context import RunContext class InMemorySessionStore(CoreSessionStore): def __init__(self) -> None: super().__init__() self.sessions: dict[tuple[str, str], RunContext] = {} async def _load(self, user_id: str, session_id: str) -> RunContext | None: return self.sessions.get((user_id, session_id)) async def _save(self, ctx: RunContext, info: SessionInfo) -> None: self.sessions[(ctx.user_id, ctx.session_id)] = ctx async def _list(self, user_id: str) -> list[SessionInfo]: return [ SessionInfo( user_id=ctx.user_id, session_id=ctx.session_id, title="Example session", message_count=len(ctx.messages), ) for ctx in self.sessions.values() if ctx.user_id == user_id ] async def _delete(self, user_id: str, session_id: str) -> bool: return self.sessions.pop((user_id, session_id), None) is not None async def main() -> None: store = InMemorySessionStore() context = await store.load("user_ana", "demo") or RunContext(user_id="user_ana", session_id="demo") agent = Agent( name="Assistant", description="An assistant with a custom session store.", instructions="Answer in English.", client=OpenAIChatCompletionClient(model="gpt-5.6-luna", api_key="YOUR_API_KEY"), ) async with agent: response = await agent.run("Hello.", run_context=context) await store.save(response.context) print(response.final_text) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main())

Python Copy """Create a teaching embedding with three word counters.""" import asyncio from max_ai.base.embedding import CoreEmbedding class TopicEmbedding(CoreEmbedding): @property def model_id(self) -> str: return "topic-counter-v1" async def _embed(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]: temas = [ {"bank", "interest", "money", "investment"}, {"food", "recipe", "cooking", "ingredient"}, {"code", "python", "programming", "software"}, ] return [ [float(sum(palabra in texto.lower().split() for palabra in tema)) for tema in temas] for texto in texts ] async def main() -> None: vectors = await TopicEmbedding().embed(["investment and money", "cooking recipe"]) print(vectors) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main())

Python Copy """Store a local workspace in another folder that represents a backend.""" import asyncio import shutil from pathlib import Path from max_ai.base.workspace import WorkspaceBase class FolderWorkspace(WorkspaceBase): def __init__(self, root: Path, backend: Path) -> None: super().__init__(root=root) self.backend = backend async def download(self, user_id: str, conversation_id: str | None = None) -> None: local = self.materialize(user_id, conversation_id).workspace_dir remote = self.backend / user_id if remote.exists(): shutil.copytree(remote, local, dirs_exist_ok=True) async def upload(self, user_id: str, conversation_id: str | None = None) -> None: local = self.materialize(user_id, conversation_id).workspace_dir shutil.copytree(local, self.backend / user_id, dirs_exist_ok=True) async def main() -> None: workspace = FolderWorkspace(Path("./local/agents"), Path("./local/backend")) folder = workspace.materialize("user_ana").workspace_dir (folder / "note.txt").write_text("A note stored in the workspace.", encoding="utf-8") await workspace.upload("user_ana") print(Path("./local/backend/user_ana/note.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main())
